- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 3–5% relative to model output.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline, it often overcorrects; cap forecast peak at 1.5x recent high or adjust downward by 2–4% after spike.
- In sentiment-neutral or bearish (≤0.33) periods, model underestimates downside risk; add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows to account for mean reversion.
- When sentiment shifts from bearish to bullish mid-horizon, model often lags; adjust forecast 2–3 days ahead to reflect sentiment momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early period (first 7–10 days) if sentiment is bullish; reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 1–2% to align with historical mean reversion.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.33” or “0.67” patterns, model often misreads sentiment direction; use sentiment average over last 5 days as a smoothing filter before forecasting.
